chunks: They think the allied tribes have not withdrawn; and if the allied tribes had advanced they would have wished that they were rather with the Arabs of the desert asking news of you; and had they been among you they would have fought but just a little.
ai.seo_question: Why did the allies of the Confederates hesitate to fight the Muslims during the Battle of the Trench?
ai.summary: Ibn Abbas and other exegetes interpret this verse as exposing the superficial nature of the confederate alliance, where tribal loyalty to Quraysh was outweighed by self-preservation. This psychological fragility underscores the Shia understanding of *Nifaq* (hypocrisy), illustrating how external pressure reveals the true, weak resolve of those who lack deep faith. The verse serves as a historical precedent for analyzing the cohesion of Muslim communities during times of existential threat.
